concepts.title: Similarity of Polygons
concepts.definition: Two geometric shapes with the same number of sides are similar if all corresponding interior angles are identical and the lengths of all corresponding sides share a common ratio.
concepts.key_idea: Matching angles line up and every pair of corresponding sides keeps one constant ratio.
question_patterns: Are all circles similar?
Are all squares similar?
State whether two given quadrilaterals are similar or not
What are the two conditions for similarity of polygons?
Give two examples of non-similar figures

solution_steps.action: Check if the number of sides is equal
solution_steps.explain: Both polygons must have the same number of sides to be compared for similarity.

solution_steps.action: Verify corresponding angles
solution_steps.explain: Ensure that all corresponding interior angles of the two polygons are equal.

solution_steps.action: Verify ratio of corresponding sides
solution_steps.explain: Check if the ratio of the length of each side of the first polygon to the corresponding side of the second polygon is constant.

concepts.title: Basic Proportionality Theorem Segment Calculation
concepts.definition: When a line is drawn parallel to one side of a triangle, it cuts the other two sides in equal ratios, allowing the determination of any single missing segment length.
concepts.key_idea: The parallel line divides the two sides in the same proportion.
question_patterns: In triangle ABC, DE is parallel to BC. If AD is {segment_a}, DB is {segment_b}, and AE is {segment_c}, find EC.
Find the length of EC when DE is parallel to BC and other segments are given
Calculate the missing segment AD using Thales theorem
What is the value of the unknown segment in a triangle divided by a parallel line?
Determine the length of segment_d given the other three proportional segments

solution_steps.action: Calculate the ratio of division
solution_steps.explain: Find the ratio of the two segments on the first side of the triangle.

solution_steps.action: Calculate the missing segment
solution_steps.explain: Multiply the third segment by the ratio of division to find the missing segment length.

solution_steps.action: Verify the segment lengths satisfy Thales theorem
solution_steps.explain: Confirm that segment_b / segment_a equals segment_d / segment_c, ensuring the parallel line divides both sides proportionally.

concepts.title: Converse of Basic Proportionality Theorem
concepts.definition: If a straight line cuts two sides of a triangle in equal ratios, then that line must run parallel to the third side of the triangle.
concepts.formula: AD / DB == AE / EC implies DE || BC
concepts.key_idea: Equal ratios of division imply parallel lines.
question_patterns: State whether EF is parallel to QR
Verify if the line dividing the sides is parallel to the base
Use the converse of BPT to check if DE is parallel to BC
Show that the line joining points on two sides is parallel to the third side
Is the line parallel to the third side if the segment lengths are given?

solution_steps.action: Calculate the ratio of segments on the first side
solution_steps.explain: Divide the first segment by the second segment on the first side.

solution_steps.action: Calculate the ratio of segments on the second side
solution_steps.explain: Divide the corresponding first segment by the second segment on the second side.

solution_steps.action: Compare the ratios
solution_steps.explain: If the two ratios are equal, then the line is parallel to the third side.

concepts.title: AA and AAA Similarity Criteria
concepts.definition: Two triangles are similar if their corresponding angles are equal, which is guaranteed if at least two angles of one triangle match two angles of the other.
concepts.formula: angle_A = angle_D and angle_B = angle_E implies triangle_ABC ~ triangle_DEF
concepts.key_idea: Angle equality is sufficient to establish similarity between triangles.
question_patterns: Prove that two triangles are similar using AA criterion
Find the angle in a similar triangle using angle sum property
Show that triangle POQ is similar to triangle SOR
Are the two triangles similar by AAA similarity?
Identify if the triangles are equiangular and similar

solution_steps.action: Identify two pairs of equal angles
solution_steps.explain: Look for given angles, vertically opposite angles, or alternate interior angles.

solution_steps.action: Apply the AA similarity criterion
solution_steps.explain: Since two angles of one triangle are equal to two angles of another, the triangles are similar.

solution_steps.action: Conclude the third angle is equal by the angle sum property
solution_steps.explain: Since the sum of angles in a triangle is 180 degrees, equality of two angles forces the third pair to be equal, confirming AAA similarity.

concepts.title: SSS Similarity Criterion
concepts.definition: Triangles are similar if the ratios of all three pairs of corresponding sides are equal, which consequently makes their corresponding angles equal.
concepts.formula: AB / DE = BC / EF = CA / FD
concepts.key_idea: Proportionality of all three sides ensures similarity.
question_patterns: Check if two triangles are similar using SSS criterion
Find the unknown angle in a triangle similar by SSS
Verify similarity of triangles when all side lengths are given
Show that the ratio of corresponding sides is constant for similar triangles
Are these triangles similar based on their side ratios?

solution_steps.action: Compute the ratios of all three pairs of corresponding sides
solution_steps.explain: Divide the lengths of the corresponding sides of the two triangles.

solution_steps.action: Verify if the three ratios are equal
solution_steps.explain: If all three ratios are equal, the triangles are similar by SSS.

solution_steps.action: Conclude the corresponding angles are equal
solution_steps.explain: Equal side ratios imply equal corresponding angles, so the triangles are similar by SSS similarity criterion.

concepts.title: SAS Similarity Criterion
concepts.definition: If one angle of a triangle equals an angle of another triangle, and the sides enclosing these angles are proportional, the triangles are similar.
concepts.formula: AB / DE = AC / DF and angle_A = angle_D
concepts.key_idea: One equal angle between two proportional sides guarantees similarity.
question_patterns: Prove similarity of triangles using SAS criterion
Are the triangles similar if one angle and its adjacent sides are proportional?
Show that triangle AMC is similar to triangle PNR using medians and SAS
Verify if the triangles are similar by SAS similarity
Determine if the given triangles satisfy the SAS similarity condition

solution_steps.action: Identify the equal angle in both triangles
solution_steps.explain: Find one angle in the first triangle that is equal to an angle in the second triangle.

solution_steps.action: Calculate the ratios of the sides enclosing these angles
solution_steps.explain: Divide the lengths of the two enclosing sides of the first triangle by the corresponding enclosing sides of the second triangle.

solution_steps.action: Check if the enclosing side ratios are equal
solution_steps.explain: If the ratios are equal and the included angles are equal, the triangles are similar by SAS.

concepts.title: Indirect Measurement of Heights using Shadows
concepts.definition: The height of a tall object can be calculated by comparing its shadow length with the height and shadow length of a shorter vertical pole at the same time.
concepts.key_idea: The ratio of height to shadow length is constant under the same sun angle.
question_patterns: A vertical pole of length {height_pole} m casts a shadow {shadow_pole} m long and at the same time a tower casts a shadow {shadow_tower} m long. Find the height of the tower.
Calculate the height of a tower using shadow lengths
What is the height of the tower if a pole of height {height_pole} casts a shadow of {shadow_pole}?
Find the height of a building given its shadow and a reference pole
How high is the tower when the shadow lengths are known?

solution_steps.action: Calculate the ratio of the tower shadow to the pole shadow
solution_steps.explain: Divide the shadow of the tower by the shadow of the pole.

solution_steps.action: Multiply by the pole height to find the tower height
solution_steps.explain: The tower height is the pole height multiplied by the shadow ratio.

solution_steps.action: Verify the height-to-shadow ratio is consistent
solution_steps.explain: Confirm that height_tower / shadow_tower equals height_pole / shadow_pole, ensuring the sun angle is the same for both objects.

concepts.title: Dynamic Shadow Length of a Walking Person
concepts.definition: Determines the length of a person's shadow after walking away from a lamp-post at a constant speed for a given duration.
concepts.key_idea: Using similar triangles formed by the lamp-post and the person to find the shadow length.
question_patterns: A girl of height {girl_height} m is walking away from the base of a lamp-post at a speed of {speed} m/s. If the lamp is {lamp_height} m above the ground, find the length of her shadow after {time} seconds.
Find the shadow length of a person walking away from a lamp-post
Calculate the length of the shadow after {time} seconds of walking
How long is the shadow of a girl walking at {speed} m/s away from a lamp of height {lamp_height}?
Determine the shadow length using speed, time, lamp height, and person height

solution_steps.action: Calculate the distance walked
solution_steps.explain: Multiply speed by time to find the distance from the lamp-post.

solution_steps.action: Find the ratio of lamp height to person height
solution_steps.explain: Divide the height of the lamp-post by the height of the person.

solution_steps.action: Subtract one from the height ratio
solution_steps.explain: The proportion is based on the difference between the total base and the shadow.

solution_steps.action: Calculate the shadow length
solution_steps.explain: Divide the distance walked by the adjusted ratio.

In Fig. 6.17 (ii), DE || BC. Find AD when DB = 7.2 cm, AE = 1.8 cm, EC = 5.4 cm.

In Fig. 6.18, if LM || CB and LN || CD, prove that AM/AB = AN/AD.
In Fig. 6.19, DE || AC and DF || AE. Prove that BF/FE = BE/EC.
In Fig. 6.20, DE || OQ and DF || OR. Show that EF || QR.
In Fig. 6.21, A, B and C are points on OP, OQ and OR respectively such that AB || PQ and AC || PR. Show that BC || QR.

Using Theorem 6.2, prove that the line joining the mid-points of any two sides of a triangle is parallel to the third side.
ABCD is a trapezium in which AB || DC and its diagonals intersect each other at the point O. Show that AO/BO = CO/DO.
The diagonals of a quadrilateral ABCD intersect each other at the point O such that AO/BO = CO/DO. Show that ABCD is a trapezium.
State which pairs of triangles in Fig. 6.34 are similar. Write the similarity criterion used by you and write the pairs of similar triangles in symbolic form.

Diagonals AC and BD of a trapezium ABCD with AB || DC intersect each other at the point O. Using a similarity criterion for two triangles, show that AO/OC = OB/OD.
In Fig. 6.36, QR/QS = QT/PR and angle 1 = angle 2. Show that triangle PQS is similar to triangle TQR.
S and T are points on sides PR and QR of triangle PQR such that angle P = angle RTS. Show that triangle RPQ is similar to triangle RTS.
In Fig. 6.37, if triangle ABE is congruent to triangle ACD, show that triangle ADE is similar to triangle ABC.

In Fig. 6.38, altitudes AD and CE of triangle ABC intersect each other at the point P. Show that: (i) triangle AEP ~ triangle CDP, (ii) triangle ABD ~ triangle CBE, (iii) triangle AEP ~ triangle ADB, (iv) triangle PDC ~ triangle BEC.
E is a point on the side AD produced of a parallelogram ABCD and BE intersects CD at F. Show that triangle ABE is similar to triangle CFB.
In Fig. 6.39, ABC and AMP are two right triangles, right angled at B and M respectively. Prove that: (i) triangle ABC ~ triangle AMP, (ii) CA/PA = BC/MP.

CD and GH are respectively the bisectors of angle ACB and angle EGF such that D and H lie on sides AB and FE of triangle ABC and triangle EFG respectively. If triangle ABC ~ triangle EFG, show that: (i) CD/GH = AC/FG, (ii) triangle DCB ~ triangle HGE, (iii) triangle DCA ~ triangle HGF.

In Fig. 6.40, E is a point on side CB produced of an isosceles triangle ABC with AB = AC. If AD is perpendicular to BC and EF is perpendicular to AC, prove that triangle ABD is similar to triangle ECF.
Sides AB and BC and median AD of a triangle ABC are respectively proportional to sides PQ and QR and median PM of triangle PQR. Show that triangle ABC is similar to triangle PQR.
D is a point on the side BC of a triangle ABC such that angle ADC = angle BAC. Show that CA^2 = CB * CD.
Sides AB and AC and median AD of a triangle ABC are respectively proportional to sides PQ and PR and median PM of another triangle PQR. Show that triangle ABC is similar to triangle PQR.
